meta.warning: This is a scripted demo guide, not a live AI model or clinical decision system. No chat request is sent to a service.

records.question: How do I record a measurement?
records.answer: Start by checking the crew member, the source, and the units. How to record walks through writing a number down. This page does not teach you how to place a sensor.

records.question: Why is blood pressure different?
records.answer: For {{name}}, blood pressure on this page is {{systolic}}/{{diastolic}} mmHg. The average of the previous {{window}} days is {{systolicBaseline}}/{{diastolicBaseline}} mmHg. It is marked when either number differs by more than 10 mmHg. Usual, Different, and Flagged are labels in this console, not a medical status.
records.actionLabel: See where the numbers come from

records.question: Why is heart rate different?
records.answer: For {{name}}, heart rate on this page is {{heart}} bpm. The average of the previous {{window}} days is {{heartBaseline}} bpm. It is marked when the difference is more than 10 bpm. This is not a diagnosis.
records.actionLabel: See where the numbers come from

records.question: What is my blood sugar?
records.answer: For {{name}}, blood sugar on this page is {{glucose}} mg/dL. It comes from the stored day, or from the check-in if you saved one this visit. Blood sugar is not part of the Usual, Different, or Flagged label.

records.question: Why do I feel tired?
records.answer: For {{name}}, how tired is {{fatigue}} out of 5. The average of the previous {{window}} days is {{fatigueBaseline}}. It is marked when today is more than 1.5 higher than that average. This is what was written down. It is not a medical grade.

records.question: What is my temperature?
records.answer: For {{name}}, temperature on this page is {{temperature}}°C. Blood oxygen is {{spo2}}%, and breathing is {{respiration}} breaths a minute. These follow the check-in when you save one. They are not part of the Usual, Different, or Flagged label, and this page does not diagnose a fever.

records.question: Explain my example baseline.
records.answer: For {{name}}, the latest demo sleep value is {{sleep}} hours and the example baseline is {{sleepBaseline}} hours. The baseline is the rounded mean of the previous {{window}} synthetic mission days for that crew member, excluding today. It is not a clinical reference range or a model trained on NASA medical records.

records.question: What does perceived effort mean?
records.answer: The exercise log uses a simple subjective demo scale: 1 means very light effort and 10 means extremely hard. Its mean summarizes entries; it does not establish safe exercise intensity or diagnose recovery. Review workload alongside sleep, fatigue, and the actual mission-approved exercise plan.

records.question: How do routine reminders work?
records.answer: The routine checklist tracks actions completed in this demo run. Reminders use an in-page timer with selectable demo intervals, snooze, and dismiss. They do not run reliably after the page closes or the browser suspends it, and the timing is not a NASA medical schedule.

records.question: What changes in another mission environment?
records.answer: Your selected context preview is {{context}}. It changes educational notes about gravity, communication, and hazards. The recorded source mission and synthetic readings do not change, and the app does not alter baselines or thresholds merely because a different environment is selected.

records.question: Is the body overview a scan?
records.answer: No. The body overview is an interactive schematic that groups available demo values by topic. It does not scan the body, measure an organ, localize disease, or derive new health findings from an image.

records.question: Where do these numbers and explanations come from?
records.answer: The health values come from synthetic JSON fixtures and temporary demo input. NASA HRP pages provide educational context, not the fixture numbers, comparison rules, or validation of this software. OSDR, live sensors, and actual astronaut medical records are not integrated.

safetyResponse: This educational demo cannot assess urgent symptoms, diagnose a condition, or recommend medications or doses. In actual operations, do not rely on this prototype: follow the established mission emergency procedures and contact trained crew or mission medical support through the available channels.
fallbackResponse: I only have the written topics listed here. I can explain this person's heart rate, blood pressure, sleep, how tired, blood sugar, and temperature. I cannot diagnose or recommend a treatment. Choose a topic, or open How to record.
